urls.description: In Geneva 128 states postponed the word «binding» by two years: human control remains a formula that names nobody.
urls.title: Who says no on our behalf

data.text: https://t.co/ctRBFbNh2L

note_tweet.text:
One hundred and twenty-eight states spent a week in Geneva on killer robots and came out with a verb: the text will be «elaborated» by 2028, not negotiated.
Ninety-eight of them had asked for a binding instrument, 163 had voted for it at the UN. The deferral costs the delegations nothing and everyone else two more years.

The formula everyone signs is «meaningful human control over the use of force», and it names nobody. The human can be the officer who decides, or the one who ratifies a computed target with a click and a timestamp. In the second case control exists, is documented, and contains no refusal: it is a signature, and a signature establishes who answers, not what is stopped.

The threshold being fought over, «full autonomy», is the wrong one. The worst damage happens below it, where the human stays in the loop precisely so the killing stays attributable.

The only wall raised this month is not a law but a company. Anthropic says it lost federal contracts for refusing mass surveillance and autonomous weapons; the Pentagon calls those limits «ideological». A supplier's conscience depends on who owns the model. Protect it, and do not mistake it for a guarantee.

One act of opposition was enough, because the CCW decides by consensus. The question is not what the weapons will decide: it is whether we write a law where «no» still exists, or one where «no» has become a formula everyone can sign because it obliges no one.

urls.description: The top places at the Hermes hackathon are not new capabilities but gates: the agent that wins is the one that knows how to stop.
urls.title: Hermes: the plugins that win are the ones that slow the agent down

data.text: https://t.co/TBIn6DM5Ux

note_tweet.text:
Seven of the top eight projects at an AI agent hackathon add no new capability. They add a brake.
The people building closest to the models have stopped asking what an agent can do, and started asking how you prove what it did while nobody was watching.

The Hermes Agent Plugin Hackathon closed on 11 November with 1,508 pull requests counted by an independent tracker, 743 already merged, and 20,000 dollars paid out on Friday. The volume is not the story. The ranking is.

First place went to Foreman: it reads the real diff before every commit and blocks an agent that deletes or skips a test, rewrites the check command, or slips in a secret. A second model reviews what the rules cannot see, and a person approves the merge from Telegram.

Third was Plan Mode, which freezes every tool that can change the project until you say yes. Fourth Seedguard, keeping seed phrases and 2FA codes out of the model context. Sixth Mandate, least-privilege credentials for cron jobs. The one exception, second place, turns old phones into voice speakers: charming, and not what the judges rewarded.

The hook declared by the most entries, 388 projects, was pre_tool_call: developers are crowding where a decision is about to become an action, the last point where someone can still say no.

A green test suite that the agent repaired itself is not evidence, it is a promise. These plugins make that promise checkable by somebody else.

urls.title: The ETF record is real, but it carries a 30 September date

data.text: https://t.co/z6kG50IsMx

note_tweet.text:
356,491 bitcoin in institutional hands: an all-time high, according to filings that photograph 30 September.
Since then bitcoin has lost about a quarter and 2.9 billion dollars have left US spot ETFs in thirteen sessions, eleven of them outflows — the record describes money that was already leaving.

I ran both numbers today because the headline carried only the first. The Galaxy Research count of 13F filings is accurate: managers added 49,229 bitcoin in the third quarter, closing three consecutive quarters of net selling, and declared positions reached 29.78 billion dollars.

Then it stops being a story about quantity and becomes one about who is left. Half the net increase came from advisers and wealth platforms, 144,307 BTC in all, the ninth consecutive quarterly gain, bought while institutions were selling. Hedge funds went from 50.6 percent of declared positions at the end of 2024 to 19 percent; basis and relative-value funds fell from a peak of 101,826 BTC to 34,053. Fewer traders rotating leverage, more advisers billing fees.

A 13F sees long positions at quarter-end, only on accounts the manager decides for. It cannot see hedges and it understates the wealth channel. So the record is real and retrospective, the outflow is real and recent: the strong hand has not left, it has stopped adding.

Whether that is a pause or a reversal, the fourth-quarter filing will say. Nothing before it will.

note_tweet.text:
6,5 miliardi di dollari di ingiunzione non sono 6,5 miliardi recuperati: su bitcoin ed ether il tribunale di Abu Dhabi non ha nessuno a cui ordinare di bloccare un saldo.
Il diritto, sul denaro on-chain, arriva solo dove c'è un portiere — e il portiere, quasi sempre, è un'azienda privata.

Il 18 novembre i tribunali dell'Abu Dhabi Global Market hanno emesso un worldwide freezing order contro gli autori non identificati del furto del 29 ottobre. L'importo nel titolo è il tetto dell'ordine, non il bottino ritrovato.

I documenti del giorno dopo dicono il resto: 192 cripto-asset rubati su 11 reti. Le stablecoin valgono 3,46 miliardi, il 55% del bottino, perché USDT e USDC hanno un emittente che può congelare un saldo. Bitcoin ne vale 1,42 e un emittente non ce l'ha: c'è la catena, che non esegue ordinanze.

L'ordine si notifica sulla blockchain, verso indirizzi e non verso persone, su una lista di 26.000 wallet aggiornata nel tempo. Diciotto società, tra cui Circle e BitGo, devono tenere fermi i blocchi. Chi detiene asset sopra i 50.000 dollari li dichiara sotto giuramento entro il 30 novembre; il 1° dicembre si decide se prorogare.

Il conto vero, oggi: tra 2,7 e 2,85 miliardi congelati o sequestrati secondo il Dipartimento di Giustizia e la stima di Elliptic, meno della metà. Binance ha già coperto i clienti con 6,34 miliardi di fondi propri: rimborsare è contabilità, recuperare dipende da corti e tempi.

Recuperare non è un problema tecnico. È un problema di giurisdizione.

urls.description: The World Bank Group will study regulated stablecoin payments for development aid with Citi and Circle. It is an exploration, not a launch.
urls.title: The World Bank Tries USDC for Aid: The Boring News That Matters

data.text: https://t.co/ZrGVBmmAWW

note_tweet.text:
Ninety-six countries and more than 350 projects: the World Bank Group will study paying out aid in regulated stablecoins, with Citi and Circle.
The money that reaches a clinic or a farmer may soon travel on a blockchain rail instead of a chain of correspondent banks, and nobody outside the institution has been asked what that means.

On 17 November the group committed to exploring dollar-denominated stablecoins for payments and settlements to its clients. A study, not a launch: no roadmap, no amount, no pilot country. Citi brings the banking connections, Circle the ability to mint and settle in USDC, and the initial model stays intermediated, limited to borrowing countries where digital assets are permitted.

Ajay Banga put the stakes concretely: if the money arrives earlier, a clinic gets built on time and a farmer is paid before the harvest ends. Meanwhile bitcoin sits near 64,600 dollars, down 12.6% in a week, and US spot ETFs lost 239.9 million dollars in net outflows on 17 November.

The honest reading is that a stablecoin does not delete the checks. It moves them: to whoever issues the currency, to how the reserves are held, to who answers when minting stops. Those are the same questions development finance has asked its intermediaries for decades, now aimed at a new one.

What changes for the person receiving aid is what I will keep counting, because it never shows up in a token chart: how many days pass between a budget line and a working hospital.

urls.description: Two attacks in 24 hours that came through third parties: infected scripts on 178 sites and 27,000 Trezor orders exposed. The perimeter is the supply chain
urls.title: Nobody Breached Trezor or the BBC: Their Suppliers Got Breached

data.text: https://t.co/y3C4A1xRrQ

note_tweet.text:
178 organisations served visitors a script that swapped wallet addresses inside the browser, and none had been breached: the JavaScript came from their A/B testing vendor.
If you typed a card number into one of those pages, the form was the brand's and the code was someone else's.

Optimizely Web delivered the infected snippet from https://t.co/e2qApjKEus, a domain every customer already trusted. Report URI examined 1,611 snippets: 188 were infected and the payload was rebuilt 26 times in a day. Ledger, BBC, CNN and Salesforce are on the list, each with the attacker's code inside its own experiment field while the rest of the file arrived from the vendor.

The code replaced Bitcoin, Ethereum, Tron, Solana, Ton, Litecoin, Bitcoin Cash and Dogecoin addresses, checksums validated, clipboard included. It took card numbers typed into the page, not those inside payment iframes.

In the same 24 hours Trezor said its courier, Skladon, had lost about 27,000 orders from 9 August to 7 November: names, phones, addresses, emails, products, prices. No wallet backups, no PINs. Third supplier breach in a year, after ShipMonk and Brevo.

The money moved is small, 2,300 to 7,000 dollars by different counts. What lasts leaves no trace on a blockchain: a leaked shipment log ties a name, an address and the fact that the person holds crypto.

A firewall defends a perimeter that no longer exists. Every vendor, every CDN, every courier sits inside it now, including the ones nobody chose to review.

urls.title: Bitcoin at $62,000: the Week It Lost the 200-Day Average

data.text: https://t.co/Yyt3qkFCw3

note_tweet.text:
Twenty-five per cent of Bitcoin's value is gone since 21 October, and on Sunday the price touched 62,112 dollars, the lowest since 14 July.
The sellers are the regulated ones: almost three billion dollars left US spot ETFs in two weeks, and seventeen billion of stablecoin supply disappeared in a month.

Before the low there were two lines the market had learned to read as structure rather than opinion: the 200-day average, lost around 73,000 dollars, and the 200-week average, at 67,992 on 14 November. It took one weekend of forced selling to find out they were opinions.

Coinglass counted about two billion dollars of liquidations in 24 hours, 774 million on Bitcoin and 488 on Ethereum, mostly longs. Glassnode still sees a cluster of potential liquidations between 59,500 and 62,600, just under the lows, which is why Monday's rebound to 64,700 closes nothing.

Leverage explains the speed. The exit explains the depth: seven consecutive sessions of redemptions from the spot ETFs, 1.07 billion in the last week alone, and a stablecoin supply that shrank by seventeen billion in a month, which means cash left the system and not just the chart.

Two statements circulating in the same hours, from Michael Saylor and the chief executive of Strive, are not facts: no filing, no quantity. I left them out. The price is confirmed three times; the explanation is still a hypothesis, and only the first one deserves a headline.

Five companies leave MSCI's global indexes after the close on November 30, and one of them holds uranium rather than bitcoin.
A private committee just defined what counts as a company, and passive money follows that definition without a vote.

Alongside Strategy go Japan's Metaplanet, Upexi, Britain's Yellow Cake and Iceland's Skel Fjárfestingafélag. Yellow Cake is the tell: if this were a verdict on bitcoin, a uranium holder would have no place on the list.

The mechanism is dull, which is the point. MSCI checks whether at least half of a company's assets are operating; anyone short is measured on five ratios and fails if four do. A name already in the index leaves only if it fails in both of the last two fiscal years.

JPMorgan put the passive selling at about 2.8 billion dollars. Strategy answered with its own count: MSCI-linked funds held around 13 million shares, 3.1% of common stock, less than a day of trading. MSTR fell 1.65% after hours, small for news that sounded epochal.

An index exit is not a delisting. The shares keep trading and nobody is forced to sell a single coin. What changed is the definition.

Bitcoin sits near 73,500 dollars, and US spot ETFs closed the week to November 6 with 1.28 billion of outflows, the worst since June. Demand built on a benchmark can withdraw twice: through the funds that replicate it, and through the people who bought it to own the asset.

Whoever defines a company has already voted. The market votes next.

Top-20 status bought no protection: a billion dollars of daily volume, and the tap closed anyway.

The choke point is not the chain, it is the bank at the other end. On a centralised exchange, the intermediary's legal residence is counterparty risk, not an administrative footnote.

Seventy million POL, five addresses, one fixed block: a network votes today on whether to rewrite a balance worth 6.8 million dollars.
If Polygon's fork passes, immutability stops being a property of the chain and becomes a threshold someone can cross, and this time it is written down in public.

The document is more honest than I expected. Before the mechanism, six conditions: incidents acknowledged by the victims, the block applied by every producer, a meaningful sum, clear on-chain tracing, an explicit request from the victims, no competing claims after disclosure. It also says the quiet part: extreme action, not a general-purpose recovery tool.

The blacklist was already central control, only silent: producers read it at startup, so every change needs a release and a restart, entries never expire, and it filters only external senders.

The attacker kept pushing, offering 219,450 POL in fees and money to validators to move a transfer.

What I watch is the price of the precedent: 6.8 million is small for a chain that moves billions, and a small sum is what makes a precedent cheap to invoke next time, when the victim is less respectable or the tracing less clean.

I read the PIP and agenda myself. The vote is at 14:30 UTC.

note_tweet.text:
Six hundred and forty-three million dollars left US spot bitcoin ETFs in one Friday, taking out 63 percent of a year of net inflows.
The money of people who never touched an exchange was the first to move.

The theft was 6.3 billion dollars, attributed by the FBI to the North Korean group TraderTraitor. Three days later the bill is legible in numbers I checked myself.

BlackRock's IBIT lost 233.7 million, Fidelity's FBTC 201.4, and the assets of the funds slipped below 100 billion. Less than one percent of the holdings actually left: analysts call it a sentiment shock. It is not a run, it is everyone deciding in a few hours that the risk budget was too large, with bitcoin at 78 thousand dollars doing the rest.

Binance reopened withdrawals on Sunday at 06:00 UTC. By 03:30 it had processed 4.6 billion of outflows against 1 billion of deposits. For a day the only question an exchange had to answer was how much you are allowed to take, and it answered by itself.

Then the part no headline carries: 242 million moved through Tron in two days, 194 of it out through bridges, 48 million via Relay, 44 via THORChain, 32.1 via Chainflip. Tether froze 378.7 million and 249 million still had to move. THORChain stopped swaps on ten chains over a bug unrelated to the hack: a reorg credited a payment it never received, and it paid 10 ETH twice.

What these figures measure is not the size of the theft. It is how fast a machine can move money, and how slowly an institution can say no.
